verdict: Second read agrees with the first on the essay and disagrees on how much to touch. It is mechanically clean (no forbidden word, the only em-dashes are inside the verbatim Whitehead and Perry definition, the only exclamation is inside Luke 19:42, plain headings, contractions present) and the argument is his. Three small edits are worth making: one restated antithesis in the Amos paragraph, one epigram closer after the Lincoln quotation, one vague framing sentence in the Eisenhower paragraph. Five first-reader findings are dropped because the sentence was doing real work or the replacement was no better. The thin first-person paragraph is a real weakness that only James can fix.

keep.quote: The privilege didn't exempt Israel from judgment. It was the reason for the judgment.
keep.tell: 'It is not X. It is Y.' antithesis restating a point the paragraph has just made
keep.why: The paragraph's first sentence already says the covenant made Israel 'more accountable, not less', the verse then says it with 'therefore', and this pair says it a third time in a second antithesis. The same section has three more balanced contrasts. The first reader was right about the tell but cut the wrong sentence: the lead is plain and sets up the verse, and its proposed replacement ('what that covenant meant') was a vague framing sentence. Collapsing the after-pair keeps the gloss on 'therefore' and removes the echo.
keep.replacement: The privilege was the reason for the judgment.

keep.quote: "The Almighty has His own purposes." That is civil religion standing beneath God instead of beside Him.
keep.tell: Aphoristic preposition-swap closer; one of eight 'That is / That's' verdict sentences in the essay
keep.why: The paragraph already said civil religion at its best 'could place the nation under judgment' and that Lincoln 'declined to claim God for the Union'. The epigram restates that as a slogan after the quotation has landed. Ending on Lincoln's own words is stronger than any replacement sentence, so this is a cut, not a rewrite (the first reader's replacement restated the point again).

keep.quote: Still, the sentence people remember tells us something. Faith was prized as a national asset,
keep.why: 'Tells us something' announces that a point is coming instead of making it; BRIEF.md lists vague framing sentences among the tells earlier judges caught. Folding it into the next sentence loses nothing.
keep.replacement: Still, in the sentence people remember, faith was prized as a national asset,

dropped: "Amos told Israel that the covenant made them more accountable, not less." -- tell is real, but the replacement ('Amos told Israel what that covenant meant.') is itself a vague framing sentence. Kept the lead; trimmed the restating pair after the verse instead (see keep 1).

"This doesn't settle how a Christian should vote. It settles something prior, which is where the love of country sits." -- a real distinction at a true hinge (voting versus the order of loves), the shape VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md itself models. The replacement is stiffer, not more human.

"I came to faith out of atheism. A Christianity that seems to exist to bless one country..." -- the stub is real, but 'and I know that' turns the fact into a credential and edges back toward the personal-memory claim the ledger records as cut because it could not be confirmed. Left for James (for_james 1).
"What the data describe is less a kind of devotion than a kind of belonging." -- 'consider' finding. The devotion/belonging contrast is the research finding itself; the replacement deletes it.
"A Christian can love America deeply and still know..." -- 'consider' finding. 'Deeply' is doing concessive work here (however much he loves it); not worth an edit.

"That's the place from which a Christian can love America well." -- 'consider' finding. With the Lincoln closer cut the 'That is' pattern is no longer loud, and 'A Christian can love America well from there.' is flatter and less clear.
for_james: The one first-person paragraph ('I came to faith out of atheism.') is thin because an earlier memory clause was cut as unconfirmed. If you remember how flag-and-cross Christianity looked to you before you believed, one true sentence there would do more than any edit. Nobody should write it for you.
'it will cost something in this one' is true but unspecific. A real cost you have paid or seen a pastor pay would make the line yours; only you can supply it.
'My own tradition ought to know better than most' plus the Baptist history tells the reader you are Baptist. That is confirmed and no convention is named; confirm you want it.
The criticism of the left is one linked sentence. Your voice standard refuses false symmetry and the subject justifies unequal space, but the call is yours.
